name: apple-m3-max-40c
nominal_note: [S] Apple's tech specs give 400GB/s of memory bandwidth for the 16-core CPU, 40-core GPU M3 Max (support.apple.com/en-us/117737)
note: Measured on a 40-core, 48 GB M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) by tools/profile_writer.py with the Apple9 matrix tile. sibling_order keeps the default "either" (the writer carries it over from the file; engine.note's "the probes'" assumes a probe-derived value): p11 favors bus-first on this chip, p12 (5) reverses it once the ALU-bound op runs as long as the bus-bound one (108 %), and a paired serve A/B of bus_first against either (two rounds, the 27B with its DSpark drafter) showed no gain. With the accelerator on, the large NVFP4 and BF16 GEMVs at T = 1 run on its rows kernels: plain decode of the 27B was level (55.3 to 60.4 ms per token against 60.1 to 61.0 with it off, overlapping ranges over three paired rounds of 128 tokens), and a 10-token prompt pass took 168 ms against 1.8 s. threadgroups_per_core 2, the writer's pick at a 4 % margin, decodes the 27B level with 1: 54.4 to 54.8 ms per token against 54.3 to 55.0 (three paired rounds on the shipped kernel choices). accelerator_min_t is 2 for NVFP4 and BF16, set by hand over the 4 and 8 of the writer's October 14 run, which timed the tile without its K-split (the writer's K-split runs 16a, 16b and 25a priced the start on the autotuner's pick, which starts the tile at 2 for both; the writer now prices it on the unsplit tile, and in run 25c the pick would start BF16 at 4: its TM 8 row, 0.510 ms, is 3.2 % over the T = 2 pass's 0.494 against the 3 % margin): in a paired serve A/B of the DSpark round (two alternating rounds, the best of each arm's second and third requests, 128 tokens) the 27B decoded math at 82.3 to 83.2 tok/s against 75.1 to 76.6, chat 40.5 to 41.2 against 37.3 to 37.6 and text 34.4 to 34.5 against 33.1 to 33.9, with code level. These 2s also govern the NVFP4 and BF16 shapes the kernel choices do not list, which serve runs on the unsplit tile at two threadgroups per core, unmeasured end to end. In the same A/B, 1 threadgroup per core decoded no faster (chat 36.1 to 36.9 tok/s). FP8 keeps 4, the October 14 run's start, over the 2 that the autotuner's pick gives in runs 16a, 16b, 25a and 25c: a separate paired A/B of the same design with FP8 from T = 2 (2026-10-15, the same tokens in both arms) decoded chat at 36.0 to 37.1 tok/s against 39.9 to 40.3 and text at 31.20 to 32.65 against 32.68 to 33.84, with code and math overlapping, although on the writer's shape the tile with its K-split costs 1.010 T = 1 passes against the T = 2 shader's 1.204 and the autotuner times the two the same on the 27B's FP8 shapes. INT4 keeps 8, the October 14 run's start, unmeasured end to end on this chip (the A/Bs above served the NVFP4 27B): with the K-split its TM 8 row (1.515) costs less than the T = 4 shader pass (2.344), the start calibration.accelerator_plan's rule picks from these rows, and the writer's K-split runs time it level with or below the T = 2 pass (1.44 against 1.47 and 1.46 in 16a and 16b, 1.421 against 1.424 in 25a, 1.283 against 1.334 in 25c), but serve compiles INT4's shapes, which the kernel choices do not list, on the unsplit tile at two threadgroups per core, the writer's crew2; the October 14 run timed the unsplit tile at one per core, at 2.610 at TM 8 against the T = 4 shader pass's 2.344, and the writer now records every geometry (tile_geometry_ms) and prices INT4's start on crew2 (runs 16a, 16b, 25a and 25b predate that). A refresh prices accelerator_min_t on crew2, the unsplit tile at this chip's two threadgroups per core and serve's tile on every shape the kernel choices do not list: run 25c, a dry run after that change (its threadgroup probe tied and kept two per core), timed crew2 at TM 8, 16 and 32 at 1.50, 2.47 and 4.89 T = 1 passes for NVFP4, 1.24, 1.56 and 1.86 for BF16, 1.34, 1.91 and 3.75 for FP8 and 1.94, 2.99 and 5.75 for INT4, and would write a start of 4 for all four (BF16's by the noise margin: its TM 8 crew2 row, 1.24, is within 3 % of the T = 4 pass's 1.22; the pick would start NVFP4, FP8 and INT4 at 2 and BF16 at 4) over the hand-set 2, 2, 4 and 8, so test_m3_max_40c_keeps_its_hand_set_values fails on a refresh until the values are restored or measured again. engine.accelerator is on from this note's A/Bs (the rows GEMVs: plain decode level, a 10-token prompt pass 168 ms against 1.8 s; attention auto with its MMA kernel at T >= 4; the DSpark round), and a refresh carries it over because it also gates paths the writer does not time: it changes only by a hand edit with an A/B, and a refresh of this file must price all four formats with the tile, so a --formats subset, --no-accelerator or a --shape one format's tile refuses writes nothing. cost_T's accelerator rows are set by hand from the tile with its K-split, the geometry the kernel choices give the shapes they list (serve runs other shapes, INT4's among them, on the unsplit tile): on the writer's 17408x5120 shape on 2026-10-15, in units of the same session's best T = 1 shader pass, TM 8, 16 and 32 cost 0.890, 1.428 and 2.766 for NVFP4 (K-split 8, 4, 4), 1.046, 1.109 and 1.249 for BF16 (4, 2, 8), 1.010, 1.096 and 2.063 for FP8 (4, 4, 4) and 1.515, 2.078 and 3.538 for INT4 (2, 2, 8), where the writer's October 14 run, on the unsplit tile, wrote 1.958, 3.169 and 6.934; 1.372, 1.741 and 2.511; 1.593, 2.370 and 5.210; and 2.610, 4.074 and 8.046. The writer times the tile in each geometry the autotuner tries and keeps the autotuner's pick as cost_T's rows; its used runs 16a, 16b, 25a and 25c (25b overlapped another workspace's GPU tests and is discarded; all five are in tools/bench/results/apple-m3-max-40c_profile-writer-ksplit-runs.json) put the pick's TM 8, 16 and 32 at 0.86 to 0.92, 1.37 to 1.48 and 2.67 to 2.88 for NVFP4, 1.02 to 1.10, 1.08 to 1.16 and 1.24 to 1.32 for BF16, 1.02 to 1.04, 1.13 to 1.16 and 2.11 to 2.21 for FP8 and 1.28 to 1.44, 1.87 to 2.09 and 3.37 to 3.79 for INT4, and every row above lies in its range or within 6 % of it, less than the runs' own spread (up to 13 %). Only compiler.emit.verify_costs reads them (verify='cost'; serve verifies a fixed length), and a refresh writes its own run's rows over them. attention auto runs v3 below T = 4 and, with the accelerator on, the mma kernel at T >= 4 for head_dim 128 and 256 (compiler.emit); the writer timed v1 to v3 only, at 32 query heads where the 27B has 24, and the serve A/B of v1 against auto is the evidence for that range: an 11,281-token prompt's cold first token took 91.2 s with v1 against 76.1 s with auto, and its decode went from 27.0 to 32.2 tok/s. Against v2 (October 15, with this configuration's engine block), plain decode of the 27B after an 8,000-token prompt took 61.5 to 64.4 ms per token with auto against 64.9 to 66.2 with v2 and its prompt pass 51.8 to 52.0 s against 60.6 to 60.8 s (two alternating rounds of 128 tokens; the outputs differ at one punctuation token), and at the 27B's attention shape (24 heads, 4 KV heads, D 256, one query row) gqa_bench timed v3 at 0.100 ms per layer against v2's 0.310 over 1,024 keys, 0.301 to 0.303 against 0.336 to 0.339 over 4,096 and 0.401 to 0.550 against 0.629 to 0.632 over 16,384, with its two rounds disagreeing over 32,768. The writer's T = 1 attention timings in this file (v3 at 0.088 ms over 4,096 keys) are below what that run and the October 15 writer run this configuration replaces (commit 9ce1de5: 0.304 ms) measure for the same kernel; replayed through a refresh, that run sets attention to v2, and a contract test pins auto.

engine.note: written by tools/profile_writer.py from the kernel harnesses (min-of-N over >= 2 GB streamed per point): cost_T = the pass cost relative to a T = 1 shader pass at the best geometry per T; accelerator_min_t = the smallest T at which the unsplit tile at threadgroups_per_core (crew at one per core, crew2 at two), the tile serve runs on the shapes the kernel choices do not list, costs no more than that shader pass plus the noise margin (a tie goes to the tile); accelerator_<fmt> = gemm_tile at TM rows in the geometry the autotuner picks (crew and crew2 timed at one and two threadgroups per core, the K-splits 2/4/8/16 and their cacheless twins), in the same unit, which compiler.emit.verify_costs reads: a session without autotuning, which runs the unsplit tile, and a tuned crew2 on two threadgroups per core cost more than these rows say; the accelerator switch, which gates paths the writer does not time, is the file's (off in a new one), sibling_order and max_cb_ms are the probes' (p11, p6/p6b) and attention_rows the file's: they carry over. On this chip accelerator_min_t and the accelerator_<fmt> rows are set by hand: NVFP4 and BF16 from 2 by paired A/Bs, FP8 and INT4 at the October 14 run's 4 and 8, and the rows from the tile with its K-split; sibling_order keeps the file's default; the top-level note gives the measurements

hosts_target_model_note: 21 GB of weights against recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize 37.44 GB, maxBufferLength 28.08 GB
